notes: Shared multiplayer, three arenas, progression, Factions, replays and an expanded cosmetic collection. Weapon Balance 9.0 and existing account progress remain intact.

Fixed: Bots stop initiating fire immediately when their observed opponent moves behind cover or dies, while preserving last-seen memory and reaction time.
Bots use a loaded sidearm when their primary has no ammunition or reserve, including longer engagements.
Dash and reload wait for the authoritative match start, preventing countdown actions from carrying into combat.
The in-game crosshair remains white in both hipfire and ADS under the current theme.
Old tournament simulation checkpoints retain their reviewed compatible progression helpers after the multiplayer update.
Party changes and blocking cancel obsolete queued groups through both socket and HTTP controls; unavailable saved worlds or invalid loadouts cannot enter a shared match.
Multiplayer acknowledgements remain reliable under snapshot backpressure, and ended matches reduce presentation traffic.
Delayed connections cannot restore another account's party, chat or statistics; queue entry synchronizes the selected loadout first.
Live background matches and shared human matches reserve the same persistent bot pool; stale or disconnected background slots wait safely before resuming.
Offline practice preserves lifetime careers, weapon statistics and bot learning, including time played and equipment counters.
Server restarts drain multiplayer connections and save match checkpoints before closing account storage.
Shared official tournaments use one authoritative calendar and persistent bot roster, with eligible human-team entry and private participant earnings.
Resolved hit feedback belongs to each human shooter and preserves combined shotgun damage regardless of the server owner's display preference.
Solo mode selection, shared custom-match entry and queue errors work through existing multiplayer controls.
Player models and labels disappear when authoritative visibility hides them; spectator views retain full match visibility.
Ended background slots select a fresh matching map revision on restart instead of reusing the prior arena revision.
Party voice connects when players enable it together and safely reconnects after microphone sessions change.
Random Custom slots select available persistent bots without double-booking active matches.
Operator models refresh the correct identity, palette and team when actor slots are reused between matches.
Installed startup recognizes the new saved map settings migration and retains bounded progress diagnostics.
Custom objective/tier setup does not create persistent career scopes or return session actors to the permanent waiting pool.
Gun Game weapon switching, stale projectiles, abandonment and tied placements obey the authoritative tier progression.
Play Again retains the completed mode, and objective team colors follow the current player or spectator perspective.
Configured limited-time games retain separate career and weapon scopes; XP-only events do not enter Combined Stats or permanent-mode seasons.
Custom controls and spectator entry remain responsive, and shared mode preparation hydrates actual tier/objective state before entry.
Authenticated Ranked reward claims and equipped selections survive reconnect/restart without duplicate items or Arena Credits. Account Level, competitive Rank and unique Combined Stats stay separate.
Configured reward artwork loads correctly, and owned Ranked appearances remain selectable even after leaving the Store sale catalog.
Saved-account startup recognizes the Ranked migration and retains clear progress through a verified, recoverable update.
Ranked resets remain server-owned; account save uploads cannot fabricate rating or reward eligibility.
Trusted account exports from older schemas remain compatible with new Ranked records, preserving historical progress during migration.

Replay recording avoids match-time save pauses, preserves match navigation and each player's equipped appearance, and recovers interrupted captures safely. Closing a loading replay cannot reopen it over the lobby.

Results present the actual winning Deathmatch operator or winning team and MVP using their recorded appearances and selected victory poses. All operators retain identical gameplay hitboxes and no cosmetic changes combat statistics.
New: Human Team Deathmatch, Deathmatch, Ranked TDM and Ranked Deathmatch use separate shared-server queues and authoritative combat/results.
Persistent lobby parties support ready states, leader queue controls, invitations and reconnect.
Phone Friends adds player search, requests, privacy-aware presence, party invitations and blocking.
Human party, match and team chat includes mute, block and report controls. Deathmatch has no team chat.
Opt-in party/team voice supports push-to-talk, peer mute/volume and supported audio-device selection.
Foundry Crossing adds compact workshops, short crossings and flanking routes; Relay Fields adds longer lanes, covered crossings and relay landmarks. Brightfield Blocks remains permanent.
Separate casual, ranked, tournament, limited-time and custom map pools support seasonal rotation without removing historical maps.
Casual queues offer a short pre-match map vote; custom matches can select any eligible arena.
Gun Game advances through every current weapon tier; a final-tier kill wins, with explicit timeout ties and reconnect preservation.
Domination adds A/B/C capture objectives; Hardpoint adds a scheduled rotating scoring area across all three arenas.
A configurable limited-time mode framework supports active dates, map pools, team size, rules, allowed loadouts and independent XP/stat eligibility. No seasonal event is activated.
Custom supports every permanent mode while preserving session-only statistics.
Click Account Level to inspect the authoritative Levels 1–50 track, current XP, next-level requirement and lifetime XP.
Ranked inspection adds rating history, season/career best, completed season ranks and server-verified leaderboards while preserving the current 26-rank ladder and dimensional emblems.
Configured Ranked reward tracks support profile icons, banners, victory poses, operator appearances, weapon badges and explicitly configured Arena Credits, with persistent claim and ownership states.
Every registered weapon has independent Levels 1–10 mastery, resolved combat progression, configured challenges and cosmetic tier badges. Loadout opens the per-weapon mastery record.
Factions adds persistent social membership, Owner/Officer/Member roles, curated configurable logos, applications, invitations and faction profiles.
Completed eligible matches can be watched from Profile Replays with recorded match-era maps, loadouts and combat outcomes.
Ten distinct operators: two Basic, two Detailed, three Cool Detailed and three Premium. Obsidian, Aegis Prime and Specter cost 2,500 Arena Credits each.
Twelve profile icons, eight profile banners and six victory poses. Quiet Confidence is owned by default; other cosmetics require ownership.
Improved: Shared-server snapshots reuse the existing arena simulation, weapons, renderer and mode-specific HUD. Casual and custom matches retain eligible persistent bot fill.
Server result receipts preserve historical progress and apply new XP, ELO and completion credits once. Custom matches remain excluded.
Loading, reconnect and duplicate connection handling preserve one participant and one completed result.

Existing TDM and Deathmatch profile tabs, Ranked and Combined Stats, bot records and Weapon Meta include unique authoritative results without rewriting historical saves. Accepted records stay cached for offline inspection.
Eligible casual bot matches preserve weapon familiarity and career growth; later matches consume the same persistent identities and learned performance.
Every arena shares authoritative collision, navigation, safe TDM/Deathmatch spawns, spectator views and a detailed minimap/full-map view with consistent meter distances.
Map identities, revisions and unit metadata persist with match results and checkpoints; rotation avoids immediate repeats when multiple arenas are eligible.
Objective-mode bots distribute attacks and defenders, contest points and rotate early while keeping their existing personalities and visibility rules.
Mode-specific objective markers, minimaps, spectator displays, score/tier HUD and separate profile records show actual match state. Ranked remains exclusive to TDM and Deathmatch.
Ranked result screens show promotions and demotions with before/after ranks. Onboarding explains the existing rating system; Ranked remains TDM and Deathmatch only.
Ranked seasons preserve final records and support explicitly configured carry, reset or soft-reset policies without introducing a default rating reset.

Mastery progress and cosmetic claims are verified once from eligible authoritative results; Custom, practice, replay and debug sessions are excluded. Account XP, Ranked rating, bot familiarity and weapon balance remain separate.

Faction tags and logos appear in profiles and parties. Verified faction activity uses eligible unique results without combat bonuses; permissions, confirmations, invite blocking and reports protect membership.

Replay playback includes pause, restart, scrubbing, speed controls, player follow and tactical cameras; storage limits and favorites protect available disk space. Playback awards no progress or currency.
The Store separates operators, profile icons, banners and victory poses, with a link to earned weapon mastery badges. Inspection never grants ownership.

history.notes: A unified dark-green interface, reliable tournament autofill and no-show recovery, broader bot weapon sampling, and Combined Stats including official tournament games. Weapon Balance 9.0 and existing account progress remain intact.

New: Combined Stats includes accepted official tournament games alongside TDM, Deathmatch and Ranked, counting each match once. Custom, practice and test sessions remain excluded.
Improved: A shared dark-green presentation brings clearer model stages, controls, stat groups, tables and release history to Loadout, Operators, Phone, Weapon Meta, Tournaments, Store, Shop, Profiles and Settings.

Tournament rosters fill open positions with eligible persistent bots. Advance reservations let their background games finish before check-in, and absent humans receive a saved replacement at the deadline.

Bot weapon exploration uses actual samples from both background modes, with bounded opportunities for underused primaries and sidearms. Playstyle, familiarity and proven performance still influence each choice.
Fixed: Incomplete tournament state is reset once with a recoverable archive. Completed official history, accepted historical games, earnings and shared progression remain intact; the next official calendar retains its established sequence.
Tournament restart, no-show and reservation handling no longer waits indefinitely on absent participants or books one bot into simultaneous games. Genuine pool conflicts remain visible.
Combined profile ratios use unique accepted participation and raw totals; reconnect and repeated result delivery cannot duplicate contributions.
Weapon Meta range headings correctly identify meters; balance constants, projectile behavior, ratings and existing source statistics are unchanged.

history.notes: ARENA REFINED combines all ten audits: clearer match entry, balanced bot rotation, dimensional rank inspection, consistent meter statistics and scheduled aggregate-kill tournaments. Weapon Balance 9.0 adds the FAL. Accounts, careers and historical records carry forward.

Gameplay: Mode entry prepares the match behind a separate loading screen for at least three seconds, then enters the existing pre-match countdown. Cancel and Retry cannot create duplicate matches.

Four background slots run two Team Deathmatches and two Deathmatches, with 50 persistent bots, fair waiting rotation and a 15-second restart cooldown. Tournament reservations take priority without duplicating bots.
Tournaments: Skirmish Challenge Tournament runs every three calendar days at 7:30 PM Eastern, following daylight saving and the existing event anchor. Quarterfinals end at 7:53 PM, semifinals at 8:18 PM and the final at 8:59 PM.

Each scheduled game accepts check-in for 90 seconds inside two minutes of preparation. Fixed starts, roster locks, the first countdown and reconnect checkpoints share the saved schedule. Teams finishing early wait.

Play all three quarterfinal and semifinal games and all five final games. Aggregate team kills determine advancement; total team damage breaks a tie. Exact damage ties await an explicit ruling. Each game retains its 50-kill target and five-minute limit.

Absent humans are replaced by eligible persistent bots for the rest of the event; the replacement owns that slot’s payout. Events missed while the local authority is closed are cancelled without results or rewards.
Connected brackets, sortable team and player leaderboards, schedules, upcoming events and official history use persisted tournament records. Historical formats and custom names remain intact.
Profiles: Click a 3D ranked emblem to inspect actual Ranked Stats, rating progress and the complete current ladder.

Combined Stats counts unique casual TDM, casual Deathmatch and Ranked TDM matches once. Ratios use raw totals; official tournaments, custom matches and practice stay separate. Missing historical measurements are identified.
Presentation: AK47 magazine ribs remain seated throughout rotation and reload. Lobby operators breathe subtly while their separate weapon rotates through a full turn.
Loadout bars use red through green to compare performance, retain exact numbers and invert lower-is-better values. Combat panels use neutral surfaces while preserving team colors.
All 26 ranked emblems have shared, dimensional 2.5D assets. Weapon ranges and travel speed display in meters and meters per second without resizing the arena or changing physical range behavior.
Weapon Balance 9.0: Adds the semi-automatic FAL to the 15-weapon armory, bot selection, familiarity, audio, models, loadouts and statistics. Preferred engagement range is 48.61 m.

Applies the supplied Balance 9.0 values. The separate Weapon Balance entry lists exact numeric before/after changes. Previous patch telemetry archives once; lifetime statistics, careers and familiarity remain intact.
Fixes: Upcoming official events no longer disappear at season boundaries. First-game countdowns, saved series totals, check-in deadlines and replacement records survive restart without duplicate rewards.
Custom team invitations remain editable while the roster is incomplete; background tournament allocation no longer takes a bot between invitations.
Updated application assets activate through the existing launcher and cache workflow, with recoverable migrations and stage-specific startup errors.
Large saved worlds report verified backup and migration stages during desktop startup. Active preparation can finish before authentication; stalled stages remain bounded and identifiable.
Removed: Messages, conversation generation, conversation tools and connection settings are retired. Phone keeps Live Scores, Spectate, Bot Leaderboard and Bot Weapon Meta. Retired data is backed up before removal; bot personalities and combat behavior remain.

history.notes: OVERCLOCK improves operator faces and refines Store to distinctive appearances. Existing owned skins remain available. Sandbox adds a 50-cent Polar Camo test offer; payment service setup is still required. Weapon Balance 8.0 is unchanged.

Improvements: Refined exposed faces, head shapes and face-cover connections while preserving operator identities.
Store now offers Containment, Aegis and Monarch. Basic recolors and slight variations are retired from sale; existing owners keep every appearance and style.
Shop: A separate $0.50 Polar Camo test offer uses verified Sandbox payment to deliver the appearance once, without granting credits. Test ownership stays separate from regular ownership.
Checkout reports incomplete service setup clearly. Public real-money payments remain unavailable.

history.notes: OVERCLOCK adds Maximum FPS, adjustable HUD size, Arena Credits and 35 operator appearances. Public money checkout remains unavailable; match rewards await result verification. Weapon Balance 8.0 is unchanged.

New Features: Maximum FPS offers 60, 120, 144, 165, 200, 240, 300, 360 and Unlimited. Changes apply immediately without changing simulation timing.
HUD Size adjusts match information, the minimap and spectator controls from 75% to 140%, with live preview and Reset. Aim and reticle size stay unchanged.
Store adds 35 operator appearances, including three signature collections with an alternate style and lobby pose. Inspect, confirm and equip through your account; original operators remain free.

Arena Credits use a separate account wallet with safe purchase retries and cached owned appearances for offline play. Standard and Ranked match reports remain pending until result verification is available.
Shop lists six one-time USD credit packs. Public money checkout remains unavailable; isolated test purchases use a separate wallet and ownership.
Improvements: Fixed scenery transforms are reused between frames while preserving map geometry, shadows and cutaways.
Lobby navigation adds Store and Shop below Play, with a compact Arena Credits balance. Account controls and all four Settings tabs stay in place.
Appearance models load when viewed and use the existing animation and preview system. Gameplay rules, team indicators and weapon balance stay unchanged.
Test checkout tracks pending and delivered orders across reconnects. Returning from a payment page never grants credits by itself.

history.notes: BLUE CIRCUIT adds Ranked TDM, a separate ELO ladder, rank crests, clearer progression and equipment cards, and competitor conversations grounded in current game data. Weapon Balance 8.0 is unchanged.

Gameplay: Ranked TDM adds a separate 26-rank ELO ladder for players and named bots, with ranked streaks and match-by-match reward breakdowns.
Official tournament participant reservations prevent overlapping appearances.
Progression: A 5,000-damage reward tier and exact fractional scoring join the existing XP system. Existing levels, XP thresholds, careers and discovery history carry forward.
Separate Level and Ranked panels, modeled rank crests and clearer Profile and result progress. Match receipts retain rewards across retries and reconnects.
Equipment: Every weapon and operator card has independent rotation, Reset and zoom controls. Operators face forward unarmed; equipped weapons keep their separate showcase.
Weapon stat bars pair consistent comparisons with exact values and an optional advanced sheet.
Presentation: Self-hosted Inter and Oxanium improve headings, messages and numeric readability while preserving the blue interface and existing wordmark.
Messages: Bot contacts react as competitors, with distinct voices and their own rivalries, weapon opinions and tournament feelings.
Direct factual replies use current scoped leaderboards, ranked results, weapon data and public events. Unsupported answers stay in the existing retry flow.

history.notes: SKYLINE brings a focused lobby, five Phone apps, separate player and bot weapon statistics, a light-blue identity and a clearer tournament hub. Weapon Balance 8.0 is unchanged.

New Features: Phone now contains Messages, Live Scores, Spectate, Bot Leaderboard and Bot Weapon Meta, with compact and expanded statistics views.
Human and bot Weapon Meta use separately attributed participant statistics. Previous mixed records are retained; accurate cohort collection begins with SKYLINE.
Exit Game saves locally before closing the desktop game, with an honest close-window message in unsupported browsers.
Improvements: A simplified Play menu and six lobby choices. Player Profile and Settings are available from your username menu.
A new original wordmark and SA emblem, with a consistent navy and light-blue interface.
Own-team blue and opponent red indicators use your local perspective; neutral spectating keeps a stable team mapping.
A clearer tournament hub, event filters, registration details, brackets and per-player earnings.
Settings now has Game, Audio, Account and About tabs. Data Management is in Account; updates, release history and the player guide are in About. Player-facing debug settings are removed.

history.notes: Version 1.9 startup repair safely completes desktop updates and preserves your account, world and progression. Weapon Balance 8.0 is unchanged.

Bug Fixes: Desktop updates close the required local service before replacing application files, preventing incomplete installations.
Startup identifies the failed loading stage, checks the installed release and supports a clean Retry.
The startup screen remains visible for at least three seconds and waits for essential initialization. Optional scenery and audio do not hold up entry.
Existing worlds retain a recoverable original before progression migration; failed loading never substitutes an empty world.

history.notes: Version 1.9 adds persistent account XP, Levels 1–50 and a clean startup presentation. Weapon Balance 8.0 remains active.

New Features: Account XP and Levels 1–50, with an expandable match XP breakdown.
Level progress beside the lobby title and in your player profile. Official tournament matches earn ×1.3 XP.
Gameplay: Team Deathmatch plays to 60 kills. Automated match slots wait 15 seconds between games.
Improvements: A three-second startup presentation prepares your game while it loads.
Smarter adaptive opponents, improved weapon-meta adaptation and contextual chase behavior.
Bug Fixes: Mode-aware Deathmatch HUD and smoother bot movement and pathfinding.
Existing game caches activate automatically at startup while preserving account data.

history.notes: Tactical Adaptation improves observed-information decisions, team coordination, contextual finishing and current-patch weapon learning. Balance 8.0 and permanent progress are preserved.

Improvements: All five bot playstyles use bounded combat memory, contextual finishes, safer reloads, recovery timing and score-aware decisions. Power affects consistency and execution.

Active team Power informs delayed, uncertain team intentions, reload cover, complementary angles, regrouping and coordinated pressure. Deathmatch retains individual placement and third-party awareness.

Weapon selection develops from discovery through stable current-patch evidence, alongside playstyle, personality, range, familiarity and personal results. Earlier tactical samples and all balance history remain available.
Owner debug adds action utilities, team intentions, chase and last-known confidence, meta phase, weapon candidates and movement goals.
Bug Fixes: Finishing decisions estimate enemy health from confirmed damage; lost sight freezes the last-known position and reduces confidence.
Decision commitment and hysteresis reduce repeated action switching while allowing urgent defensive responses. Repeated failed approaches lose preference.
Bots use the same configured movement speed at every Power. Custom difficulty changes session execution without changing weapon mechanics or permanent ratings.

history.notes: Core Tuning raises standard TDM to 60, fixes the Deathmatch HUD and movement oscillation, adds a persistent 15-second slot cooldown and applies Balance 8.0 while preserving lifetime progress.

Improvements: Standard Team Deathmatch target: 50 → 60 kills. The five-minute limit and tied overtime are unchanged; custom TDM inherits 60.
Completed automated slots wait 15 seconds before the next match. Each slot keeps its own saved deadline and reserved roster across restart.
Balance: War Head LMG: projectile speed 78 → 81; shot interval 0.47s → 0.42s.
P90: headshot damage 35 → 40; shot interval 0.24s → 0.23s; reload 2.40s → 2.20s.
SR-Aug: per-bullet body damage 24 → 23; headshot damage 49 → 45. Three-round bursts retain the 0.70s cycle and 65ms spacing.
SPAS-12: combined body damage 108 → 100; combined headshot damage 220 → 210. Twelve real pellets per shell are unchanged.
Balance 7.0 telemetry is archived once; Balance 8.0 starts clean. Careers, familiarity, accounts, seasons and tournament history are preserved.
Bug Fixes: Deathmatch now shows personal kills, placement, leader kills and its 30-kill target, with mode-aware spectator and scoreboard labels. Its ten-player, four-minute rules are unchanged.
Bots update nearby path destinations without reversing around stale endpoints. Bounded replanning, safe waypoint tolerance and forward-preserving avoidance remove repeated movement corrections.

history.notes: Tactical Instinct adds situation-aware opponents, Deathmatch and flexible custom matches. Balance 7.0 and existing progress are preserved.

New Features: Deathmatch: ten participants, first to 30 kills, four-minute limit and a separate career record.
Custom matches with selected roster bots, teams, zero to nine bots, optional player participation and four session-only difficulties.
Final-five-second countdown and mode-aware results with Play Again and Lobby actions.
Delete your custom tournament, including safe cancellation of its active games and invitations.
Improvements: Opponents react to score, time, observed reloads, teammate readiness and recent combat experience while retaining their permanent Power and playstyle.
Paired pressure, supporting fire, complementary angles and bounded waits improve teamwork without changing weapon mechanics.
The upper equipped-operator showcase faces forward in a relaxed unarmed pose.
Weapon Meta separates the new tactical revision from preserved earlier samples.
Bug Fixes: Desktop updates safely restart the existing local service after replacing its files, preserving your account and world.
Completed results reject late damage and duplicate finalization; custom sessions cannot award official progress.

history.notes: Fieldcraft brings a cohesive tactical interface, richer operators, weapons and Brightfield scenery, clearer observer controls, a refined Phone, and more varied weapon audio. Balance 7.0 and all existing progress are preserved.

New Features: Select any of the four active bot matches directly from the observer controls.
Improvements: Skirmish Arena branding and a cohesive green interface across Home, Loadout, Operators, Meta, Leaderboard, Profile, Calendar, Settings and Patch Notes.
Clearer match and spectator HUDs, improved pause controls, readable feedback and consistent focus, hover and selected states.
Stronger equipment showcases and refined 2.5D geometry, finishes and gear across all 14 weapons and all eight operators.
Richer Brightfield roads, sidewalks, buildings, vegetation and neighborhood props while preserving the existing arena layout.
Four firing variations per weapon and three variations per reload phase, with distinct class sound, tactile menu cues and a clearer ambience mix.
A refined Phone shell, clearer Home, Contacts and Messages navigation, better thread presentation and more grounded competitor conversations.
Existing account data, careers, seasons, tournaments, lifetime records and Balance 7.0 telemetry carry forward.
Bug Fixes: Fresh desktop startup handles game-cache activation races and upgrades older cached startup pages without requiring Retry or clearing account data.
Repaired disconnected weapon rails, sights, scope fittings and folded-stock mounts; simplified operator gear and weapon surface detail while preserving all palettes, animations and gameplay.

history.notes: Live Circuit adds the Phone, official and custom tournaments, detailed models, improved movement and distinct weapon audio. Updates verify the active game build; careers and saves are preserved.

New Features: Phone with Messages, all contacts, Back and Home navigation.
Official tournaments every 72 hours: eight teams of five, BO3 quarterfinals and semifinals, BO5 final.
Calendar, custom tournaments, invitations, isolated results and persistent per-player prize earnings.
Improvements: 2.5D-only operator and weapon art, Blender detail kits and improved walking and sprinting.
Distinct firing, reload and handling identities for every weapon.
Personality-driven questions, complaints, reactions and tournament conversations.
Cleaner menus, public settings, README and categorized Patch Notes.
Bug Fixes: Updated launchers replace stale local services and verify actual game code after cache activation.
Standard-match completion checkpoints persist immediately and count once.
Large local worlds and retained backups now save reliably without loading stale progress.
Cursor position changes aim only; movement and ADS select exact shared projectile and reticle spread.
